''Taktakalas'' (area in old Nicosia where club is based) | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1931|6|1}} | ground = [[GSP Stadium]] | capacity = 23,000 | chairman = Petros Savva | manager = [[Georgios Kostis]] | league = {{Cypriot football updater|Olympiakos}} | season = {{Cypriot football updater|Olympiakos2}} | position = {{Cypriot football updater|Olympiakos3}} | website = {{Official URL}} | pattern_la1 = _jakochallenge2122gb | pattern_b1 = _jakochallenge2122gb | pattern_ra1 = _jakochallenge2122gb | pattern_sh1 = | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = 007711 | body1 = 000000 | rightarm1 = 007711 | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_la2 = _jakoprimera22sbb | pattern_b2 = _jakoprimera22sbb | pattern_ra2 = _jakoprimera22sbb | pattern_sh2 = | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = 00A2E8 | socks2 = 00A2E8 }} '''Olympiakos Nicosia''' ({{Langx|el|Ολυμπιακός Λευκωσίας}}, ''Olympiakos Lefkosias'') is a [[Cyprus|Cypriot]] football club based in [[Nicosia]] and competes in the {{Cypriot football updater|Olympiakos}}. The club was founded in 1931, and is a founding member of the [[Cyprus Football Association]]. The club colors are black and green. Olympiakos' home ground is the [[GSP Stadium|new GSP Stadium]], which has a 23,000-seat capacity. The team's main nickname is "mavroprasini" (the green-blacks), and the club's other nickname is Taktakalas, derived from the area of Nicosia where the club hails from. Olympiakos Nicosia has won three [[Cypriot First Division]] Championships, one [[Cypriot Cup]] and one [[Cyprus Super Cup]]. In the past the club also had track and field, basketball, volleyball, cycling, table tennis, weightlifting and futsal teams. It also in the past had an orchestra, choir and camping divisions; the latter explaining why the club's badge has a tent on it."}}
